name: manual_67383a
claim: An aggregate counter over an append-only JSONL lessons store (e.g. a dashboard's accepted-count) must not do a naive per-line status==accepted count -- retract_lesson.py appends a NEW row with the SAME id and status=retracted rather than editing the original in place, so the original accepted row is still on disk and gets double-counted forever unless the counter dedupes by id (latest row wins). Separately, supersession creates a DIFFERENT id whose supersedes field points at the old one, and the old id's row still literally has status=accepted -- so counters also need to exclude any id referenced by another accepted lesson's supersedes field, mirroring render_lessons.py's _build_auto_section pattern (only ACCEPTED supersessions retire the old lesson; a provisional supersede must not).

decisions.notes: Found via CodeRabbit PT PR #337 review 4874635749 pointing at show.py:lesson_stats() inflating the accepted count. Fixed by replicating render_lessons.py's latest-by-id + superseded-id-exclusion logic inside lesson_stats(), with 4 new regression tests (superseded, retracted, provisional-does-not-retire, unrelated-lessons-all-counted) in tests/test_show_lesson_stats.py.
